s1.syndrome_frame: Progressive weakness, fatigue, and confusion with a mediastinal mass and pulmonary emboli
salient_findings: Increasing weakness, fatigue, and confusion over a few weeks
Lobar and segmental pulmonary emboli in right middle and lower lobes
key_facts: 67-year-old man with a history of mood disorder, Parkinson's disease, hyperlipidemia, and mild cognitive impairment
Presented after an unwitnessed fall at home
Family noticed increasing weakness, fatigue, and confusion a few weeks before presentation
Patient reported decreased appetite and mild dyspnea, especially on exertion
No significant weight loss, dysphagia, or odynophagia
No history of smoking
Elevated serum creatinine: 3.7 mg/dL (327 μmol/L)
Hemoglobin: 10.5 g/dL (105 g/L)
α-fetoprotein and β-human chorionic gonadotropin levels: normal
CT head and C-spine: unremarkable
CT chest: lobulated anterior mediastinal mass
Contrast CT chest: showed lobar and segmental pulmonary emboli in right middle and lower lobes
MRI brain with and without contrast: no intracranial mass lesion
Immunohistochemistry: Positive for P40 immunostain
Negative for thyroid transcription factor-1 and napsin A immunostains
